top.title: What Kirby Smart said about Glenn Schumann's FSU football interest
top.description: Kirby Smart provided a brief comment on the future of No. 1 Georgia's defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann and his potential future as Florida State football's head coach. Speaking during a Monday, Nov. 23 press conference, the Georgia head coach was asked directly if he's had any conversations with Schumann about his potential move to take over as head coach of the Seminoles (5-6, 3-5 ACC). His response was brief. "Schumann has done a fabulous job here, and anything that comes from his success; he has earned every bit of it," Smart said. "But the University of Georgia is focused on Georgia Tech ." Short and sweet from Smart. But despite his avoidance, Schumann remains the Seminoles' frontrunner for the vacant head coach role, which became available after Mike Norvell was fired Nov. 1 . The university and Schumann have met to discuss the role, and multiple reports suggest that the two parties are close to an agreement. He has emerged as the lead candidate early in the Seminoles search, and his connection with now FSU athletic director Jeff Purinton could be playing a key role. Schumann and Purinton crossed paths at Alabama when Schumann started working as an undergraduate assistant under Nick Saban before he eventually followed Smart to Georgia. Schumann has earned a reputation for being an elite recruiter and developer of talent with the Bulldogs. One such example of that is linebacker Justin Williams. The former 5-star prospect who Schumann recruited to Athens spoke about the potential departure of his defensive coordinator when asked. "I know nothing about it. I mean, I’m really happy for him, whatever he chooses to do. He’s a great coach, great individual,” Williams said. "I see him like a father figure to me. He’s a great guy. So whatever he wants to do, I’m happy for him.” No public announcements have been made about the future of Schumann, but he remains the frontrunner in the Seminoles search ahead of a rivalry weekend for both teams. FSU hosts Florida, and Georgia faces Georgia Tech, meaning any offcial annoucments would likely be made after the pair of games. top.title: Viral video shows Denver looking silly on Josh Giddey’s game-tying layup – but it was all part of the plan
top.description: Ron Chenoy-Imagn Images Viral video shows Denver looking silly on Josh Giddey’s game-tying layup – but it was all part of the plan appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Denver Nuggets found themselves at the center of an unusual late-game sequence during their matchup with the Chicago Bulls . A viral clip showed Josh Giddey walking into an uncontested layup to tie the score in the closing seconds of regulation, making Denver’s defense look completely lost. However, the decision behind the play was more deliberate than it initially appeared. According to The Denver Post reporter Bennett Durando, Nikola Jokić believed he was fouled before committing the turnover that led to Chicago’s basket, a concern the coaching staff shared after reviewing the footage. However, Denver’s defensive approach on the other end was intentional. Cam Johnson explained that the Nuggets would rather concede an open two-point shot than allow Buddy Hield to get a clean three-pointer. “Buddy had it going, so we did not want him to finish the game with a 3. An open one,” Johnson said. JOKIC SENDS THE GAME TO OVERTIME 🔥 pic.twitter.com/okzh23tR1t Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — BrickCenter (@BrickCenter_) November 23, 2026 The sequence unfolded after Denver lost possession late in the fourth quarter. Chicago capitalized on the turnover, moving the ball to Giddey for an easy basket with 2.1 seconds remaining. The layup sent the game into overtime at 131-131, despite the Nuggets initially appearing to have control. Rather than risk giving Hield another opportunity from beyond the arc, Denver prioritized taking away his shot, even if that meant leaving the basket exposed. The strategy ultimately worked in the bigger picture, as the Nuggets recovered and pulled away in overtime. Denver outscored the Bulls in the extra period to secure a 151-145 road victory. Josh Giddey still delivered a remarkable performance in the loss, finishing with 23 points, 14 rebounds and 22 assists. His historic night made the viral defensive sequence even more memorable, but the Nuggets left Chicago with the win. top.title: How Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley's rivalry evolved over 30 years
top.description: STORRS — When Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley share the court on Tuesday night , the focus will be on two of women’s basketball’s most storied programs. But the relationship between the Hall of Fame coaches stretches back much longer than UConn and South Carolina, beginning when Staley was the star point guard for Virginia over 30 years ago. Since then, their relationship has evolved through the two programs’ dynastic runs and reached an uncomfortable flashpoint after last year’s Final Four confrontation. UConn vs South Carolina preview: Geno Auriemma downplays Dawn Staley subplot ahead of UConn-South Carolina showdown On Sunday , Auriemma said he would prefer the attention stay on the players. “I'm just trying to coach my team because they're the ones playing, and that's what people are coming to watch,” Auriemma said on Sunday. “I think they're coming to watch South Carolina and Connecticut play against each other.” With both teams meeting for the first time since last year’s Final Four, here’s a look at the timeline of Auriemma and Staley’s relationship. Player vs. Coach Staley has been on Auriemma’s radar since she was a kid. Back in 2016, Auriemma told ESPN that he first heard about Staley when she was a basketball prodigy in Virginia. "It's like she was the original Mo'ne Davis," Auriemma said. "From the time Dawn was in seventh or eighth grade, that's all anybody was talking about in girls' basketball. She had a reputation that preceded her when she got to Virginia [in 1988], and she was part of their greatest successes as a team.” Staley went on to play at Virginia from 1988 to 1992, coinciding with Auriemma’s first few years at UConn. Staley went 2-0 in her playing career against Auriemma, helping Virginia beat UConn in the 1991 Final Four and in a nonconference matchup during the 1991-1992 season. South Carolina’s rise Staley got her start in coaching in 2000 at Temple while she was still an active WNBA player. “I was still playing in the WNBA, but I was drawn to the difficulties and opportunities of turning a struggling basketball program around,” Staley wrote in the Players’ Tribune in 2015. Staley retired from playing in 2006 after 12 years of professional basketball. She left Temple two years later to coach at South Carolina. By then, Auriemma had led UConn to five national championships and nine Final Four appearances. Over the next decade, UConn established itself as the country’s premier women’s basketball program. But even as UConn cemented itself as the sport's dominant program, Staley was building South Carolina into a powerhouse. She won national championships in 2017, 2022 and 2024 and has guided the Gamecocks to eight Final Four appearances. “The trajectory that they've made has been very similar (to us),” Auriemma said on Sunday. “It's just harder now. top.title: Rams dealt another season-ending news before Packers game
top.description: The Los Angeles Rams are preparing for a difficult stretch of their NFL schedule as injuries continue to affect their roster. Head coach Sean McVay has already faced several selection problems, particularly on offense, where the team has lost important contributors. The Rams hoped to get some injured players back after their Week 11 bye. However, those plans have not gone as expected, leaving the coaching staff with more decisions to make before Wednesday’s meeting with the Green Bay Packers. The latest setback involves a young tight end who has spent much of the season recovering from an ankle injury. His situation has now taken another disappointing turn, with his return plans effectively coming to an end. MORE: Bhayshul Tuten injury update casts doubt on Jaguars RB’s Week 12 status Terrance Ferguson ruled out for remainder of season after Rams injury setback Los Angeles Rams tight end Terrance Ferguson (18) Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Los Angeles Rams will not activate tight end Terrance Ferguson from injured reserve, according to ESPN’s Sarah Barshop. The reporter revealed on Monday, November 23, that Ferguson is still dealing with an ankle injury and will not return this season. Ferguson had been working toward a return after the Rams opened his 21-day practice window earlier in November. However, he suffered a hamstring injury during practice ahead of the team’s Week 9 game against the Washington Commanders. That setback delayed his comeback and kept him out of the lineup. Rams TE Terrance Ferguson is still dealing with an ankle and will not come off IR. He is done for the season. — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) November 23, 2026 McVay had previously indicated that the Rams planned to activate Ferguson before his practice window closed on November 25. The intention was to keep him on the active roster while he continued his recovery. Barshop’s latest update confirms that the situation has changed, ending his hopes of returning this season. Los Angeles Rams face tight end shortage before Packers matchup Ferguson’s absence creates another problem for the Rams as they prepare for Green Bay. The rookie has been unavailable since injuring his ankle earlier in the season, limiting the team’s options at tight end. Before his injuries, Ferguson had shown promise as a receiving option. He recorded seven catches for 63 yards and a touchdown across his first three games. His absence has left Tyler Higbee, Colby Parkinson and Davis Allen to handle the position. The Rams will now need their remaining tight ends to contribute against the Packers on Wednesday, November 25. top.title: Max Verstappen jokes last time he won a race like F1 Las Vegas GP it was "Mario Kart"
top.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen says the last time he won a race like the Las Vegas Grand Prix was when he was playing Mario Kart . The Red Bull driver converted pole position into his 75th grand prix win, and his third in Las Vegas, in a race that featured 352 overtakes and 35 lead changes. Asked during the post-race press conference when he had last won a race like it, the Dutchman was reluctant to answer at first: "I probably shouldn't say it. I probably should not. I remember winning one like this when I was playing Mario Kart . "Sometimes you drop back and you get drafts, and there's like a catch-up, you know? Always when you're dropping back, you go faster. So that's the last time that I felt something like this," he said. The Red Bull driver was passed for the lead time and again, mostly by Mercedes' George Russell , and hit back every time. While he managed to retake the lead, he was not able to extend his advantage and break away from the pack behind him. "It was just the tow combination with the deployment. Of course, when you are within a second, you have the overtake mode as well, and around here that is powerful. So, yeah, you could not pull away." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Asked whether he had enjoyed the race around the streets of Las Vegas, Verstappen drew a line between the driver and the spectator. "When I look at it from my racer heart, no. When you look at it as a show, spectacle, yes. I've enjoyed my repassing and everything, but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart." The race barely raised his pulse. "Even my heart rate, I was not nervous at all because, I don't know, it just felt kind of cruising out there, just trying to press the battery whenever it was correct or defend. But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, probably yes, you like it." Verstappen currently sits second in the drivers' standings. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli claimed the title at the Mexican Grand Prix but the fight for second will continue into the upcoming Qatar Grand Prix. Verstappen has a 37-point lead over Lewis Hamilton , who sits third. George Russell and Lando Norris are fourth and fifth, respectively, both on 264 points. top.title: Syracuse football: QB Steve Angeli out, Malachi Nelson starts vs Notre Dame
top.description: CHESTNUT HILL, MASSACHUSETTS - NOVEMBER 21: Steve Angeli #9 of the Syracuse Orange throws the ball against the Boston College Eagles during the first half at Alumni Stadium on November 21, 2026 in Chestnut Hill, Massachusetts. (Photo by Brian Fluharty/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Syracuse Orange will be without its starting quarterback against the Notre Dame Fighting Irish this Saturday. Syracuse Head Coach Fran Brown announced during his weekly press conference on Monday that Quarterback Steve Angeli will not play against the Fighting Irish. The Daily Orange’s Noah Nussbaum reported that Angeli had an AC joint injury. On3’s Pete Nakos reported that x-rays and imaging came back negative and that he could return for a bowl game. Quarterback Malachi Nelson will start his third game for the Orange this season. Angeli was injured after he took a sack towards the end of the first half against the Boston College Eagles in Syracuse’s last game. He was seen on the sideline with a sling. This will be the third game that Angeli has missed due to injury. He got a Plasma-Rich Platelet (PRP) shot earlier this year to his ankle and was sideline for Syracuse’s losses to Virginia and Louisville. This also means that Angeli will not get a chance to play his former team for the second year in a row. Angeli transferred to Syracuse from Notre Dame. He played in 21 games for the Fighting Irish, starting one game for the team. He started against Oregon State in the Sun Bowl in 2023, throwing for 232 yards and three touchdowns in that game. Angeli missed the Notre Dame game last year as he was still recovering from his Achilles surgery. The game saw the Orange give up 70 points for the first time in over 100 years. A late touchdown by Quarterback Joseph Filardi stopped the shutout but Syracuse still lost 70-7 in South Bend. Syracuse turns to Nelson for his third start in an Orange uniform. He started the games against Virginia and Louisville, which Angeli and quarterback Amari Odom were unavailable for. In those two games, Nelson threw for 532 yards, three touchdowns and two interceptions on 42-68 passing. Nelson came into the Boston College game for Angeli after his injury. Nelson threw for 202 yards and a touchdown on 12-26 passing. He didn’t complete the game as he wasn’t available for the last drive due to injury. Quarterback Rich Belin came in to finish it out- he threw for 40 yards on 3-5 passing. Nelson has yet to play a full game for the Orange. He has always exited games due to injury in the three games that he saw significant action. The Boston College game was the first one that Nelson was available for since the North Carolina game. Nelson missed the previous four games as he was recovering from tight-rope surgery to fix a high-ankle sprain. Nelson was the third-string quarterback before the season started. top.title: The Detroit Lions are still no one’s favorites because of September
top.description: DETROIT, MICHIGAN - DECEMBER 4: Jared Goff #16 of the Detroit Lions shares a moment with Detroit Lions head coach Dan Campbell prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Ford Field on December 04, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images For the Detroit Lions, a six-game winning streak, a high-powered offense, and a defense that’s decidedly turned things around since Week 5 isn’t enough to earn consideration from the media as one of the premier teams in the NFL. Despite being atop the NFC North, the Lions aren’t even the team to beat in their own division . How the Lions continue to fly under the radar on a national level is, on one hand, expected. They can’t outplay their geography. They don’t play in New York or California or Illinois, states home to the three biggest sports media markets in the country. They’re not “America’s Team” or the up-and-comers they were ahead of the 2023 season. The pillars of their team remain unchanged from the beginning of a run that includes three of four seasons where the Lions have started the season 8-2 or better—something the franchise had never done in the 60 seasons prior. No matter what they accomplish, preconceptions plague this team. They’re still led by the same Jared Goff everyone decided was the NFL’s Charlie-in-the-Box—the gatekeeper for the Island of Misfit Toys. Remember Charlie from Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer ? He lives on the Island of Misfit Toys because he’s named “Charlie” instead of “Jack,” believing his name is “all wrong” and that no child would ever want a second-rate Charlie-in-the-Box. So sure, Jared looks and acts just as good as the real thing, but his name isn’t Joe or Josh, the names of quarterbacks everyone else fawns over in MVP discussions. The teams of Joe and Josh are being carried by elite quarterback play, and their teams’ mediocre defenses be damned: they’re in firm control of their respective divisions. As for the Lions defense, that’s what’s going to sink their ship this season, just as it did in 2024 when the team went 15-2 and lost to the Washington Commanders in the Divisional Round. According to the pundits, this defense is still the same turnstile it was during the first month of the season, except now its without two of their top defenders in Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson— how could Detroit possibly be considered a top-10 team? In fact, their defensive core will not play a single game together this season, so consider their Super Bowl window shattered . top.title: Fresno State bowl eligible, will face Oregon St in finale
top.description: SAN MARCOS, TX - NOVEMBER 14: Fresno State Bulldogs head coach Matt Entz congratulates players on a scoring play during game featuring the Fresno State Bulldogs and the Texas State Bobcats on November 14, 2026 at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos, TX. (Photo by John Rivera/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Over the weekend the Fresno State Bulldogs got two huge pieces of news. First, they are bowl eligible for the second time in as many years under Matt Entz. Secondly, they know who their opponent will be for the flex schedule this Saturday night as the regular season comes to a close. This past Saturday saw a shootout in the Valley between the Bulldogs and the Colorado State Rams. Jayden Mandel threw three touchdowns, while Speedy Luke ran for two more in the Bulldogs’ 49-42 win over Colorado State to end a two-game losing streak, and knock out the all important sixth win in order to become bowl eligible. Fresno State racked up 265 yards on the ground, with Bryson Donelson going for 165 yards and a touchdown himself. The aforementioned Luke had 68 yards on 10 carries to go with his scores. While the offense was high flying, the defense was all over the place. Beginning with a Simeon Rice 35-yard pick six, it appeared as though Fresno State’s problems on defense were going to be solved. However, that was not the case, as the defense couldn’t stop a nosebleed on Saturday night. Nonetheless, it goes down as a win, the sixth of the season with one contest remaining. The Pac-12 at the beginning of the season had left the final week of the regular season open as a flex scheduled game. Many predicted that the Bulldogs would take on San Diego State. However, with the Aztecs’ stunner in Boise, that game fell into doubt. On Sunday it was announced that the Bulldogs’ final contest of the 2026 regular season will be a rematch of the Halloween night matchup with Oregon State. The Bulldogs took care of business in that first contest, winning 38-22. This next game, like the previous one, will be played in Fresno as it will be Senior Night for the 2026 football team. Fresno State and Oregon State will kickoff at 7 p.m. Pacific Time on Saturday night and will be broadcasted on The CW.

top.title: The Viva El Birdos Podcast – Episode 92: Interview with Brian Walton
top.description: Analyzing the Cardinals’ Off-Season Moves Insights on player decisions and future implications for the team. The off-season is a critical time for any sports team, and the St. Louis Cardinals are certainly no exception. Recent decisions, particularly those made during the non-tender deadline, have sparked discussions among fans and analysts alike. In this week’s episode of the Viva El Birdos Podcast, Jake Wood and Brian Walton dive deep into these moves and their implications for the Cardinals’ future. Non-Tendered Players One of the most significant developments was the non-tendering of Nolan Gorman and Max Rajcic. Brian Walton shares his thoughts: “I think everybody understood that Gorman’s time with the Cardinals needed to come to an end both for him and for the team.” For Gorman, who had nearly 2,000 major league plate appearances without finding his footing, this decision wasn’t unexpected. Walton mentions the potential for Gorman to rejuvenate his career overseas: “Maybe he’s a good guy to go overseas and play in Asia.” As for Rajcic, Walton notes his promising run in Triple-A but ultimately points to a lack of long-term potential at the major league level. Future of the Roster The Cardinals are looking to create flexibility as they move forward. Walton explains that the team’s actions reflect a broader strategy: “They wanted to create another roster opening, and they did that. That gives them more flexibility if they want to be a buyer in Rule Five or sign a free agent.” With significant turnover in the roster over the past few years, including the entire starting lineup from the 2023 season minus Jordan Walker, the Cardinals are in a phase of transformation. Both hosts express curiosity about how this will play out in the upcoming season. Player Development Challenges The conversation shifts to the challenges in player development, particularly regarding past draft picks. Walton and Wood discuss how the organization has struggled to maximize the potential of its players: “I think a lot of the talent that he had brought in, the player development aspect of the organization just was not up to par.” This reflection on the Cardinals’ approach highlights the ongoing challenges the team faces in developing young talent and making strategic decisions based on their performance. Looking Ahead As the off-season continues, the Cardinals are tasked with finding the right balance between protecting promising players and making room for new talent. With the Rule Five draft approaching, Walton emphasizes the importance of making sound decisions: “Act like you assume there’s gonna be a draft. Don’t try to get cute.” This episode provides a thoughtful analysis of the Cardinals’ recent moves and what they might mean for the future. nigeria.title: 2027: Armed Men Who Killed Four NDC Campaign Members Said I Was Their Target, Omo-Agege
nigeria.description: Former Deputy Senate President Ovie Omo-Agege has alleged that the gunmen who attacked his campaign team in Delta State, killing four people, repeatedly shouted his name and declared their intention to kill him. Omo-Agege, who is seeking election to the Delta Central Senatorial District on the platform of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) in the 2027 general elections, said he escaped the attack through the intervention of his Department of State Services (DSS) escorts. He spoke on Monday while appearing as a guest on Channels Television’s Politics Today . ﻿ Recounting the incident, the former deputy senate president said he heard the attackers repeatedly shouting that they wanted to kill him while opening fire at the campaign venue. “Right there at the venue, while they were shooting, we could hear them say, ‘It is Omo-Agege we want to kill. We must kill Omo-Agege.’ “But I was lucky because my DSS details were very professional. In fact, after God, the only reason I am alive today is because of the DSS operatives who were with me,” he said. Omo-Agege described the incident as a premeditated attack, alleging that there had been a build-up to the violence. He questioned why he would be singled out for elimination when several other politicians were also contesting elective positions. The former lawmaker said the attackers struck less than five minutes after he began addressing supporters at the campaign venue. According to him, he had moved towards the side of his vehicle to make eye contact with members of the audience when the gunshots rang out. “It was by divine intervention. As I was speaking, I just moved over to the side of the vehicle to be able to make eye contact with those I was speaking with. It was immediately I did that that the volley of gunshots started,” he said. The former deputy senate president said four members of his campaign organisation were killed, while about 15 others sustained injuries, with some in critical condition. In a statement issued earlier on Monday by his media adviser, Sunny Areh, Omo-Agege’s campaign organisation said he survived an assassination attempt during a campaign tour in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. Areh alleged that armed men opened fire on the senator and his entourage while he was addressing supporters during a campaign visit. The organisation called for an independent and thorough investigation by the Nigeria Police Force, while appealing to the Inspector-General of Police, the DSS, INEC, civil society organisations and the international community to ensure the safety of political candidates and their supporters. It also urged supporters to remain calm and avoid retaliation, adding that its ward-to-ward campaign activities across Delta Central would continue. nigeria.title: Caregiver Salami shot dead in US weeks before starting Nursing school
nigeria.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye A 24-year-old Togolese caregiver in Chicago, Bintou Salami, has been shot dead while returning home from work, weeks before she was due to begin nursing school. According to ABC7 Chicago, Salami was found with a gunshot wound in the 1400 block of West Chase Avenue at about 11:15 p.m. on Wednesday. She had just finished her shift at Misericordia, where she cared for people with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Ms Salami relocated from France to the U.S. in 2024 following her marriage and planned to begin nursing school in January; she is survived by her husband and son. Her killing was one of three shootings on Chicago’s North Side that night as Police said the incidents were connected. A 35-year-old man was critically wounded near the bike path by Belmont Harbor, while a 25-year-old man was later found dead at the Morse Red Line station and a gun was recovered at the station. The Cook County Medical Examiner’s Office said the man died by suicide. Salami’s coworkers described her as caring and devoted. Ashley Hespen, assistant vice president of residential services at Misericordia, said residents loved spending time with her. Friends, relatives and members of Chicago’s Togolese community gathered at a vigil to honour Salami and demand answers. As they sang the Togolese national anthem, supporters stood with her brother at the place where she was killed. “I can’t stop looking at the picture. I don’t know, like — it’s not fair,” said Nanipo Damyete, Salami’s former roommate. Amevi Avouglah, the USA country delegate for the High Council of Togolese Abroad, said Salami’s future had been cut short. “All the dreams that Bintou is carrying vanished like that in one minute! She was coming from work,” Avouglah said. Salami’s brother, Raoufou, questioned the suggestion that she was killed during a robbery, saying nothing appeared to have been taken. “The police telling me, like, somebody tried to rob her or something. nigeria.title: Osun police bust child trafficking syndicate, rescue 16-day-old baby
nigeria.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State Police Command has dismantled a suspected child trafficking syndicate and rescued a 16-day-old baby boy allegedly sold for N1.5 million in a transaction involving two suspects. The command’s Public Relations Officer, DSP Abiodun Ojelabi, disclosed this in a statement on Monday, saying two suspects had been arrested in connection with the alleged trafficking. According to the police, the baby’s mother, Victoria Michael, 18, gave birth at a private hospital in Kajola on November 2 but was unable to cater for the child after the father, identified as Tayo, allegedly denied responsibility. Ojelabi said one of the mother’s friends, Comfort Olayinka, offered to help her find assistance through a contact in Abeokuta, Ogun State. He said Olayinka subsequently linked up with Oladipo Olamide, 46, who allegedly claimed to operate a non-governmental organisation providing care for less-privileged persons and offered to take the baby into its care. The police spokesman said the baby’s mother and Olayinka travelled to Abeokuta on November 5 and handed the child over to Olamide. However, Olayinka later allegedly told the mother that the baby had died and gave her a folded object resembling a baby, packed in a bag, which she was instructed to throw into Lafenwa River. Unknown to the mother, Olayinka had allegedly collected N450,000 from Olamide, purportedly for her upkeep. Ojelabi said police operatives, acting on intelligence, arrested Olamide in Abeokuta on November 17. During interrogation, the suspect allegedly confessed to selling the baby to one Mrs Bolanle Ruth for N1.5 million. He said Olamide subsequently led the operatives to Akure, Ondo State, where Ruth was arrested on November 18. According to the police, Ruth admitted paying N1.5 million for the baby and claimed she was promised that the necessary documents would be provided by an agency, but had yet to receive them. The police did not disclose the whereabouts or status of the other suspect, Olayinka, in the statement. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police in Osun State, Ibrahim Zungura, warned individuals and groups against child trafficking, assuring residents that the command would not tolerate the crime. He urged members of the public to provide useful information to security agencies to help prevent child trafficking and protect vulnerable children. The operation, conducted on November 22 by personnel of Nigerian Navy Ship (NNS) Pathfinder around Okarki Creek and Okarki Community in Ahoada West Local Government Area, followed credible intelligence. In a statement on Monday, the Director of Naval Information, Navy Captain Abiodun Folorunsho, said the naval personnel intercepted a wooden boat conveying about 150 sacks containing suspected stolen crude oil. He said a subsequent operation in the adjoining area led to the discovery of an illegal refining site containing approximately 10 dugout pits, 180 sacks and a storage container holding an estimated 54,000 litres of suspected illegally refined AGO. According to him, the combined volume of petroleum products recovered or identified during the operation was approximately 89,000 litres. “The boat, its contents and the refining site, including the stored products, were handled in accordance with established anti-crude oil theft procedures,” the statement said. The Navy described the operation as part of its sustained campaign to disrupt the supply networks supporting crude oil theft and illegal refining activities in the Niger Delta. It said intercepting the suspected stolen crude oil and dismantling associated refining infrastructure would help deny oil thieves access to petroleum resources while addressing environmental degradation and revenue losses. The Service reaffirmed its commitment to intelligence-driven operations to protect critical oil and gas infrastructure, support national crude oil production and safeguard Nigeria’s economic interests. It added that operations would continue across the Niger Delta creeks to combat crude oil theft and illegal refining. business.title: Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Solo Bitcoin Miner Wins $191,000 Block Reward With Just 11 TH/s A solo miner running about 11 terahashes per second has mined Bitcoin block 977,057, collecting a reward of 3.1287 BTC, or about $191,000, on a machine that makes up roughly one-millionth of a percent of the network. The block was found through the solo service at CKpool on Sunday, Nov. 22, at about 7:54 a.m. ET. The reward is the 3.125 BTC subsidy plus about 0.0037 BTC in transaction fees, and it was worth roughly $191,000 at bitcoin’s price when the block landed. How the solo block played out The block holds 584 transactions. Its coinbase transaction pays 3.0661 BTC to a single address and 0.0626 BTC, about 2% of the reward, to a second output. That split matches the service’s 2% fee, which means the miner’s take is a little over $186,000. Con Kolivas, the developer behind CKpool, congratulated the miner on X, whose address he abbreviated as bc1q~zy9j. It matches the end of the address that received the payout. Kolivas called it the 323rd block found on the service and “yet another lucky one.” He said the miner had only about 11.1 TH/s of hashrate on a 3.47 TH worker. “A miner of this size has about a one in 1650 chance of solving a block in a year,” Kolivas wrote. The block was tagged to Solo CK on the mempool.space block explorer, and its coinbase carries the pool’s signature. CKpool describes itself as a service that lets miners go after full solo blocks without running their own node, since you cannot mine directly to a Bitcoin Core node. A recent run of solo wins Solo CK has found five blocks since Nov. 6, according to the explorer’s pool page . The most recent before this one was block 976,642 on Nov. 19, followed by blocks on Nov. 11, Nov. 7 and Nov. 6. Each paid between 3.13 and 3.15 BTC. Earlier this year, a different solo miner won block 943,411 on the same service on April 2, for about 3.139 BTC. In October, a FutureBit Apollo solo miner found block 973,262 and earned 3.154 BTC. Those wins are the exception. Most of the network’s hashrate sits in large pools and industrial operations that split rewards across many miners, which is how they smooth out the luck. A single small machine can run for years without finding anything, and a lucky block can show up on day one. Miners on the service get nothing unless they find a block, and then they keep the full reward minus the 2% fee. Network hashrate and difficulty Bitcoin’s network hashrate was about 1.04 zettahashes per second, or roughly 1,043 exahashes, on a three-day average Monday. The selloff came even after Nvidia reported better-than-expected quarterly results on Nov. 17. In Asali Africa’s new series, it is where the conversation starts. There’s Rice at Home is a cooking and conversation show from Asali Africa, the Lagos-based creative development agency, hosted by Chef Soliat Bada . In each episode, Soliat cooks one rice dish with a guest, and while the pot does its work, the two get into the kind of talk that usually happens around food: family, money and what success really looks like. Rice is the most ordinary thing in a Nigerian kitchen, and the show makes a good case that it doesn’t have to taste ordinary. Over five episodes, released every two weeks, the menu travels from Jamaica to Saudi Arabia, back home to Nigeria and on to Louisiana. You don’t just watch the food get made, either. The recipes are written up in full on Asali Africa’s website, with the ingredients and method laid out step by step, so you can watch Soliat cook a dish and then make it in your own kitchen. The season opens with Rice and Peas with Oxtail, the Jamaican Sunday staple of rice cooked in coconut milk with red kidney beans (the “peas”), served beside rich, slow-cooked oxtail. Soliat’s guest is Michael Famoroti , co-founder of Stears, and their conversation turns to family and black tax: the expectation that once you start earning, you start supporting the people who raised you. Read the full recipe for Rice and Peas with Oxtail . Rice and peas with oxtail, from Episode 1 Soliat Bada and Michael Famoroti in Episode 1 Episode 2 moves to the Gulf for lamb kabsa, Saudi Arabia’s national dish, fragrant with dried lime and seven spice. Soliat is joined by Bella Adeleke , CEO of Asali Africa and founder of the fashion label Garbe, for a conversation about redefining success. Read the full recipe for Lamb Kabsa . Lamb kabsa, from Episode 2 Still to come are Nigerian fried rice with fried turkey and dodo, cooked with Toyin Jolapamo and Nneoma Mere; jambalaya with Goldie Iyamu and Vanessa Iloenyosi ; and a season finale with Edwin Okolo and Temi Omolehinwa. For more on Asali Africa and the products and ideas it develops, visit asali.africa . Episodes 1 and 2 are out now on YouTube. entertainment.title: Beyond the Mini LED Label: What Should Define Good Mini LED Performance?
entertainment.description: The presence of Mini LED tells a shopper something important about the light source behind an LCD panel. It does not, by itself, explain how that light is arranged, divided or controlled. Those implementation choices can have a major influence on contrast, black level performance, highlight control and the visibility of blooming in difficult scenes. From Presence To Performance That distinction matters because a category becomes more useful to consumers when it can be evaluated through clear performance principles rather than through a technology name alone. For Mini LED, three factors provide a practical starting point. The first is hardware local dimming. In a hardware based system, physical groups of LEDs can be brightened, dimmed or switched off independently across different areas of the screen. This gives the television more direct control over how light is distributed within a single image. The second is local dimming zone count and precision. A higher number of independently controlled zones can allow the backlight to respond in smaller areas, which can improve separation between bright highlights and surrounding dark regions when other major conditions are comparable. The number itself is not the whole story, but it is a useful indicator of how granular the backlight system can be. The third is backlight architecture. Full Array Local Dimming places controllable zones across the area behind the panel, providing the physical foundation for more localized light management than designs that illuminate the panel from the edges or operate the backlight more uniformly. Together, these three elements move the Mini LED conversation from a simple question of whether the technology is present to a more useful question: how effectively is the light being controlled? Where TCL Enters The Category Conversation TCL is relevant to that discussion because Mini LED has become a significant part of its global television business. According to Omdia data cited in TCL Electronics interim results, TCL ranked No. 1 globally by Mini LED TV shipment volume in the first half of 2026. TCL reported 2.43 million Mini LED TV shipments during the period, representing 77.1% year on year growth. That position follows a strong 2025, when TCL reported, based on Omdia data, a 31.1% share of global Mini LED TV shipments and 118.0% year on year shipment growth. Market scale does not, on its own, define technology leadership. What it does provide is evidence that a manufacturer has become an important participant in how the category develops. For a company operating at that scale, leadership increasingly includes helping make the technology easier to understand and giving consumers clearer ways to evaluate what they are buying. Beyond the usual Lagos parties and end-of-year outings, there is a whole continent waiting to be explored, with sun-soaked beaches, wildlife safaris, exciting food scenes and cities with plenty of stories to tell. You do not have to spend weeks navigating embassy appointments and visa applications to make it happen, either. Several African countries offer Nigerian passport holders visa-free entry or visas on arrival, making a festive-season escape much easier to plan. Nigerian citizens enjoy visa-free entry for short stays of up to 60 days without needing a paid eTA, leaving more room in your budget for safaris and coastal stays. entertainment.description: “Men are not wired to show emotions.” A male friend once said to me during an argument. He was so convinced that I wondered whether a manual somewhere explained how men were manufactured. According to him, men were created to be strong, endure pain and keep their emotions to themselves. That was simply how they were made. “So, because you’re a man, you’re not supposed to feel hurt, fear or disappointment?” I disagreed. He insisted that showing emotions was not in a man’s nature. Who made that rule? Who decided that men could experience pain but must never be seen expressing it? At what point did being a man become synonymous with pretending that everything was fine? The conversation wilted, but it has stayed with me, perhaps because my friend wasn’t expressing an unusual opinion. He was repeating a stereotype many of us have heard all our lives: “Boys don’t cry.” “Be a man.” “Man up.” Three little expressions, and somewhere between being told to be strong and learning to say “I’m fine,” I wonder how many men have forgotten what it feels like to be heard. Frequent questions men are asked: “How far? Work nko?” “When are you getting married?” “Have you bought land?” “How is the family?” And the famous Nigerian question that can make an unemployed graduate dread family gatherings: “So, what are you doing now?” We often inquire about their achievements, responsibilities, and plans. These aspects are important, but how often do we ask about their fears? A father who leaves home before sunrise and returns exhausted, burdened by the weight of school fees, rent, and family expectations. A young graduate who has submitted countless job applications, yet still smiles politely when another relative inquires why he hasn’t found a job. A successful professional whose LinkedIn profile showcases numerous achievements, while his personal life tells a story that no one has thought to ask about. We admire their strength, we applaud their sacrifices, and we celebrate their accomplishments. But what about what they are going through? The person everyone leans on also needs somewhere to lean. Society has an interesting checklist for measuring a man’s success. A good job, a house, a car, a wife, children and financial stability. Preferably, all achieved before a certain age. But if a man struggles to achieve all these, is his life any less meaningful? Surely, a man’s worth cannot be reduced to his bank balance, job title or ability to convince everyone that he has everything under control. There must be room for men who are still becoming. It marked the brand’s first Living Lab in the country, creating a platform for more accessible conversations around skin health, dermatological innovation and everyday skincare. The experience opened with an exclusive session for healthcare professionals and invited guests before welcoming members of the public over the following two days. Through interactive demonstrations and guided product experiences, guests gained a better understanding of different skin concerns and the role of targeted skincare in addressing them. At the Anthelios corner, visitors used a UV camera to see the effects of ultraviolet exposure and better understand the importance of sun protection. The Effaclar and Mela B3 spaces explored concerns including blemishes and hyperpigmentation, while the Cicaplast and Lipikar corners introduced visitors to approaches to caring for sensitive, damaged and dry skin. Movies, as a powerful art form, present a sequence of events that allows viewers to see reflections of themselves or envision who they could become. One subject that art, particularly film, has explored is masculinity. However, this theme is often addressed subtly and can be easy to overlook, as the movies that dominate global box offices frequently focus on spectacle: fantasy, romance, adventure or others. Conversations about men, their inner lives, vulnerabilities and social roles are often not in the top circle. Through his struggles with homelessness, rejection, and exhaustion, the film redefines masculinity, depicting it as the courage to remain tender even when life tests your strength in every way. Fatherhood Kevin Hart ’s film Fatherhood delves into themes of grief and single parenthood, balancing humour with heartfelt moments. These conversations defined The Executive Woman Summit (TEWS) 2.0 , which brought together hundreds of executive women, corporate professionals, entrepreneurs and emerging leaders at Harbour Point, Victoria Island, Lagos, on Wednesday, October 28, 2026. sports.description: Kirby Smart provided a brief comment on the future of No. 1 Georgia's defensive coordinator Glenn Schumann and his potential future as Florida State football's head coach. Speaking during a Monday, Nov. 23 press conference, the Georgia head coach was asked directly if he's had any conversations with Schumann about his potential move to take over as head coach of the Seminoles (5-6, 3-5 ACC). His response was brief. "Schumann has done a fabulous job here, and anything that comes from his success; he has earned every bit of it," Smart said. "But the University of Georgia is focused on Georgia Tech ." Short and sweet from Smart. But despite his avoidance, Schumann remains the Seminoles' frontrunner for the vacant head coach role, which became available after Mike Norvell was fired Nov. 1 . The university and Schumann have met to discuss the role, and multiple reports suggest that the two parties are close to an agreement. He has emerged as the lead candidate early in the Seminoles search, and his connection with now FSU athletic director Jeff Purinton could be playing a key role. Schumann and Purinton crossed paths at Alabama when Schumann started working as an undergraduate assistant under Nick Saban before he eventually followed Smart to Georgia. Schumann has earned a reputation for being an elite recruiter and developer of talent with the Bulldogs. One such example of that is linebacker Justin Williams. sports.description: STORRS — When Geno Auriemma and Dawn Staley share the court on Tuesday night , the focus will be on two of women’s basketball’s most storied programs. But the relationship between the Hall of Fame coaches stretches back much longer than UConn and South Carolina, beginning when Staley was the star point guard for Virginia over 30 years ago. Since then, their relationship has evolved through the two programs’ dynastic runs and reached an uncomfortable flashpoint after last year’s Final Four confrontation. Player vs. Coach Staley has been on Auriemma’s radar since she was a kid. Back in 2016, Auriemma told ESPN that he first heard about Staley when she was a basketball prodigy in Virginia. "It's like she was the original Mo'ne Davis," Auriemma said. "From the time Dawn was in seventh or eighth grade, that's all anybody was talking about in girls' basketball. She had a reputation that preceded her when she got to Virginia [in 1988], and she was part of their greatest successes as a team.” Staley went on to play at Virginia from 1988 to 1992, coinciding with Auriemma’s first few years at UConn. sports.title: Max Verstappen jokes last time he won a race like F1 Las Vegas GP it was "Mario Kart"
sports.description: Motorsport photo Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen says the last time he won a race like the Las Vegas Grand Prix was when he was playing Mario Kart . The Red Bull driver converted pole position into his 75th grand prix win, and his third in Las Vegas, in a race that featured 352 overtakes and 35 lead changes. Asked during the post-race press conference when he had last won a race like it, the Dutchman was reluctant to answer at first: "I probably shouldn't say it. I probably should not. I remember winning one like this when I was playing Mario Kart . "Sometimes you drop back and you get drafts, and there's like a catch-up, you know? Always when you're dropping back, you go faster. So that's the last time that I felt something like this," he said. The Red Bull driver was passed for the lead time and again, mostly by Mercedes' George Russell , and hit back every time. While he managed to retake the lead, he was not able to extend his advantage and break away from the pack behind him. "It was just the tow combination with the deployment. Of course, when you are within a second, you have the overtake mode as well, and around here that is powerful. So, yeah, you could not pull away." Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Asked whether he had enjoyed the race around the streets of Las Vegas, Verstappen drew a line between the driver and the spectator. "When I look at it from my racer heart, no. When you look at it as a show, spectacle, yes. I've enjoyed my repassing and everything, but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart." The race barely raised his pulse. "Even my heart rate, I was not nervous at all because, I don't know, it just felt kind of cruising out there, just trying to press the battery whenever it was correct or defend. But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, probably yes, you like it." Verstappen currently sits second in the drivers' standings. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli claimed the title at the Mexican Grand Prix but the fight for second will continue into the upcoming Qatar Grand Prix. Verstappen has a 37-point lead over Lewis Hamilton , who sits third. George Russell and Lando Norris are fourth and fifth, respectively, both on 264 points. The pillars of their team remain unchanged from the beginning of a run that includes three of four seasons where the Lions have started the season 8-2 or better—something the franchise had never done in the 60 seasons prior. No matter what they accomplish, preconceptions plague this team. They’re still led by the same Jared Goff everyone decided was the NFL’s Charlie-in-the-Box—the gatekeeper for the Island of Misfit Toys. Remember Charlie from Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer ? He lives on the Island of Misfit Toys because he’s named “Charlie” instead of “Jack,” believing his name is “all wrong” and that no child would ever want a second-rate Charlie-in-the-Box. So sure, Jared looks and acts just as good as the real thing, but his name isn’t Joe or Josh, the names of quarterbacks everyone else fawns over in MVP discussions. The teams of Joe and Josh are being carried by elite quarterback play, and their teams’ mediocre defenses be damned: they’re in firm control of their respective divisions. As for the Lions defense, that’s what’s going to sink their ship this season, just as it did in 2024 when the team went 15-2 and lost to the Washington Commanders in the Divisional Round. According to the pundits, this defense is still the same turnstile it was during the first month of the season, except now its without two of their top defenders in Jack Campbell and Aidan Hutchinson— how could Detroit possibly be considered a top-10 team? In fact, their defensive core will not play a single game together this season, so consider their Super Bowl window shattered . Mind you, we all live in our own echo chambers, seeds planted on a screen where our algorithms grow around us into any shape we encourage it to take: it’s an environment as real as the world. It becomes the truth, it is the truth. So while we play part in creating these environments, it doesn’t excuse these takes as any less misinformed than they actually are. sports.title: Fresno State bowl eligible, will face Oregon St in finale
sports.description: SAN MARCOS, TX - NOVEMBER 14: Fresno State Bulldogs head coach Matt Entz congratulates players on a scoring play during game featuring the Fresno State Bulldogs and the Texas State Bobcats on November 14, 2026 at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos, TX. (Photo by John Rivera/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Over the weekend the Fresno State Bulldogs got two huge pieces of news. First, they are bowl eligible for the second time in as many years under Matt Entz. Secondly, they know who their opponent will be for the flex schedule this Saturday night as the regular season comes to a close. This past Saturday saw a shootout in the Valley between the Bulldogs and the Colorado State Rams. Jayden Mandel threw three touchdowns, while Speedy Luke ran for two more in the Bulldogs’ 49-42 win over Colorado State to end a two-game losing streak, and knock out the all important sixth win in order to become bowl eligible. Fresno State racked up 265 yards on the ground, with Bryson Donelson going for 165 yards and a touchdown himself. The aforementioned Luke had 68 yards on 10 carries to go with his scores. While the offense was high flying, the defense was all over the place. Beginning with a Simeon Rice 35-yard pick six, it appeared as though Fresno State’s problems on defense were going to be solved. However, that was not the case, as the defense couldn’t stop a nosebleed on Saturday night. Nonetheless, it goes down as a win, the sixth of the season with one contest remaining. The Pac-12 at the beginning of the season had left the final week of the regular season open as a flex scheduled game. Many predicted that the Bulldogs would take on San Diego State. However, with the Aztecs’ stunner in Boise, that game fell into doubt. On Sunday it was announced that the Bulldogs’ final contest of the 2026 regular season will be a rematch of the Halloween night matchup with Oregon State. The Bulldogs took care of business in that first contest, winning 38-22. This next game, like the previous one, will be played in Fresno as it will be Senior Night for the 2026 football team. Fresno State and Oregon State will kickoff at 7 p.m. Pacific Time on Saturday night and will be broadcasted on The CW.

sports.title: The Viva El Birdos Podcast – Episode 92: Interview with Brian Walton
sports.description: Analyzing the Cardinals’ Off-Season Moves Insights on player decisions and future implications for the team. The off-season is a critical time for any sports team, and the St. Louis Cardinals are certainly no exception. Recent decisions, particularly those made during the non-tender deadline, have sparked discussions among fans and analysts alike. In this week’s episode of the Viva El Birdos Podcast, Jake Wood and Brian Walton dive deep into these moves and their implications for the Cardinals’ future. Non-Tendered Players One of the most significant developments was the non-tendering of Nolan Gorman and Max Rajcic. Brian Walton shares his thoughts: “I think everybody understood that Gorman’s time with the Cardinals needed to come to an end both for him and for the team.” For Gorman, who had nearly 2,000 major league plate appearances without finding his footing, this decision wasn’t unexpected. Walton mentions the potential for Gorman to rejuvenate his career overseas: “Maybe he’s a good guy to go overseas and play in Asia.” As for Rajcic, Walton notes his promising run in Triple-A but ultimately points to a lack of long-term potential at the major league level. Future of the Roster The Cardinals are looking to create flexibility as they move forward. Walton explains that the team’s actions reflect a broader strategy: “They wanted to create another roster opening, and they did that. That gives them more flexibility if they want to be a buyer in Rule Five or sign a free agent.” With significant turnover in the roster over the past few years, including the entire starting lineup from the 2023 season minus Jordan Walker, the Cardinals are in a phase of transformation. Both hosts express curiosity about how this will play out in the upcoming season. Player Development Challenges The conversation shifts to the challenges in player development, particularly regarding past draft picks. Walton and Wood discuss how the organization has struggled to maximize the potential of its players: “I think a lot of the talent that he had brought in, the player development aspect of the organization just was not up to par.” This reflection on the Cardinals’ approach highlights the ongoing challenges the team faces in developing young talent and making strategic decisions based on their performance. Looking Ahead As the off-season continues, the Cardinals are tasked with finding the right balance between protecting promising players and making room for new talent. With the Rule Five draft approaching, Walton emphasizes the importance of making sound decisions: “Act like you assume there’s gonna be a draft. Don’t try to get cute.” This episode provides a thoughtful analysis of the Cardinals’ recent moves and what they might mean for the future. sports.title: Dylan Larkin breaks silence after trade to Canadiens
sports.description: Mandatory Credit: Rick Osentoski-Imagn Images Dylan Larkin breaks silence after trade to Canadiens appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The stalemate between the Detroit Red Wings and Dylan Larkin has come to an end. On Sunday night, the Red Wings traded Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens. On Monday night, Larkin will make his Canadiens debut against the Los Angeles Kings . As the former Red Wings captain prepares for his Canadiens debut, he is breaking his silence on the trade, per Habs on Reddit. “My dad is Canadian, my wife is Canadian. Montreal is such a great city, it has so much to offer. Myself and my whole support system are so excited for something new,” Larkin said. “To be in a great city like Montreal, where it means so much to put that (Habs) jersey on, with its history and the great players and great teams before.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Larkin was the 15th overall selection of the Red Wings in the 2014 NHL Draft. He made his debut with the Wings in the 2015-16 season, and has spent his entire career in Detroit. Larkin played 818 games with 278 goals and 371 assists with the Red Wings. He wore the number 71 with the Red Wings, but that number is currently worn by Jake Evans in Montreal. Instead, Larkin will be wearing number 89 for the Canadiens. Putting on that jersey is something Larkin is excited about. “I love playing in this building,” Larkin said of playing at the Bell Centre. “(To) put that jersey on for the first time in this building, it means something to me. I’m so excited for that.” Meanwhile, his new coach, Martin St. Louis, is also excited to have Larkin and is already defending him. “Marty, Larkin was in Detroit and, for lack of a better term, he sort of quit on that team. Montreal wasn’t his first choice to come to, from what was reported regarding his no-trade clause. Do those things concern you at all with him coming in?” St. Louis was asked. “I think it’s a harsh thing to say that he quit on his team. We don’t have, we only know what we think we know. technology.title: Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack
technology.description: Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers. CVE-2026-76466 , which carries a 9.8 CVSS rating, affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, both virtual and physical appliances running vulnerable software. These provide firewall traversal, VPN-less remote access, and call routing for remote users connecting to voice, video, and messaging collaboration services. The bug involves hard-coded authentication credentials and insufficient certificate validation in clustered Expressway deployments. “An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands,” Cisco said in October, when it disclosed the bug and issued a software update that fixed the flaw. “A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.” At the time, the networking vendor said it wasn’t aware of any abuse of the vulnerability. That all changed late last week, however, when Russian security firm F6 said it was investigating “the first observed case” of miscreants exploiting CVE-2026-76466, shortly after a public proof-of-concept exploit became available. “The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices,” F6’s Cyber Defense Center said on Thursday. “Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network. After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure.” Specifically, the criminals prepared custom Python code to scan the victim’s network and identify files and folders shared over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. The scripts were also designed to interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories for credentials and other sensitive information. The Python scripts used in the attack indicated that the operator used an AI assistant, according to F6. The security shop also noted that one of the key indicators of compromise is a nodeup “wombat@127.0.0.1” entry in the Erlang system log (erlang.log) on affected Cisco Expressway devices. A day later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and told federal agencies to patch by Monday. Cisco updated its advisory on Monday to acknowledge CISA’s addition, while noting that it has no direct evidence of active exploitation. The Register reached out to the networking and security vendor for additional details about the scope of the attacks, but did not receive any response. We will update this story as we learn more. ®

Alan is also a novelist—his debut novel, the urban fantasy The Sixth Borough, is available now.

Sports in space have a long and proud tradition, whether it's Alan Shepard playing golf on the moon or the crew of the ISS hosting their own version of the Summer Olympics . The future looks bright as well, with the foundation of the Space Games Federation , the self-described "first governing and sanctioning body for competitive sports played in zero or micro-gravity," co-founded by a NASA astronaut. Not to be outdone, science fiction has expanded the idea of zero-g and low-gravity sports to their logical extent, imagining everything from Doctor Who's zero-g squash to the advanced, gamified combat simulations of Ender's Game. There was even Space Jam 's alien basketball game for the fate of the planet, though the gravity-defying antics there come from cartoon shenanigans rather than a zero-g playing field. As humanity edges closer to colonizing our neighbors through projects like the Artemis Program and its ambition to establish habitats on the moon, our imaginations have to expand to encompass not only how we'll live in space but also how we'll play. The rules change when gravity disappears (Image credit: Zero-G) We rarely think about it in an Earth context, but every sport is heavily influenced by gravity. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 23, 2015: Blue Origin sticks 1st-ever rocket landing from space with its suborbital New Shepard rocket
science.description: null On Nov. 23, 2015, a Blue Origin rocket made a historic landing. Before this time, all rockets were single-use only — even SpaceX's rockets. Blue Origin changed the concept forever. After launching the New Shepard capsule safely into space, the rocket started heading back to Earth. It flew towards a landing pad, reignited its engine to slow down and touched down softly on the ground . This was the first successful vertical landing from space in history. The Blue Origin milestone meant that rockets could be reused for multiple missions, which saves money and reduces waste. (Image credit: Blue Origin) Why it mattered Today, SpaceX may be the most well-known for landing its Falcon 9 rocket boosters from orbit. The company's triple-core Falcon Heavy boosters can also land vertically and its massive Starship megarocket can even return to the launch site to be caught by giant metal arms. But in the end, Blue Origin did it first. Blue Origin's New Shepard booster landing kicked off an era of vertical launch and vertical landings for rockets that continues to this day. It may have even outlasted the New Shepard rocket. Since that first landing, Blue Origin has launched 17 suborbital astronaut flights with New Shepard, and 21 more uncrewed flights for a total of 38 missions between April 2015 and 2026. The company reused its New Shepard boosters repeatedly (though it did lose one during an uncrewed launch after a technical issue.) But in January 2026, the company announced a pause in New Shepard flights for two years so that it could focus on moon lander projects. But Blue Origin did not abandon rocket landings. Indeed, the company's success with New Shepard led it to build vertical landing into its larger orbital rocket, New Glenn, which made its first successful landing 2025 — nearly 10 years after that first touchdown. Blue Origin has since reflown a New Glenn booster , and is developing a new rocket engine called Northstar for even better performance. Want more space history? Lunar Reactor-1 (LR-1) will be a small fission power system that will generate 20 kilowatts of electricity, enough to power approximately 16 average U.S. households annually on Earth. For NASA’s plans for a Moon Base , that energy could support future habitats, communications systems, rovers, scientific instruments, and other essential infrastructure. NASA aims to have a launch-ready system by 2030 and operate it on the Moon for at least five years after deployment. Unlike solar power, which depends on sunlight, a nuclear reactor can generate electricity continuously, including during the Moon’s approximately two-week-long nights. This capability will enable future lunar operations, particularly in locations where sunlight is limited or unavailable. “This request for proposals represents an important step forward as NASA partners with industry to establish an enduring human presence on the lunar surface,” said Brian Giblin, NASA’s Lunar Reactor-1 program manager. “A reliable source of safe and abundant energy will be vital to future exploration of the lunar and Martian surface. Space nuclear systems will provide continuous power to NASA assets in any environment without dependency on sunlight.” NASA’s Space Power and Reactor Capabilities Request for Proposals incorporates feedback received after the agency released a draft proposal in August and hosted an industry day in September at the Ohio Aerospace Institute in Cleveland. The solicitation requires that the reactor must meet Department of Energy (DOE) safety standards for nuclear operations. While the primary purpose of the Request for Proposals is to advance the technology, testing, and flight design of LR-1, NASA may issue additional task orders to support the development of other space nuclear power systems. Proposals are due by Dec. 21. Nuclear power will be increasingly important to NASA’s space exploration ambitions. Lunar nights last about 14 Earth days, while dust storms on Mars can block sunlight for months. Farther from the Sun, solar power becomes progressively less effective. In particular, the rocks and mineral deposits could help researchers piece together the planet's watery past and identify environments that may once have been capable of supporting microbial life. NASA's Curiosity rover recently wrapped up a drilling campaign at a location nicknamed "Nazca," where scientists have been examining unusual disk-shaped crystal formations embedded in the surrounding bedrock. Avengers: Doomsday has been promising the scale and excitement the MCU has often been lacking since the Infinity Saga. science.description: null An image of Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, produced by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Researchers have spotted an ancient, "dead" Martian volcano from orbit around the Red Planet. What is it? The European Space Agency's Mars Express spacecraft, which has been orbiting and studying the planet since it arrived in 2003, recently captured incredible new imagery of the volcano Tharsis Tholus. This snapshot was captured by the spacecraft's High Resolution Stereo Camera. Even as old and worn as it is, the Martian volcano stands at around 4.97 miles (8 kilometers) tall which is comparable to some of the highest peaks in the Himalayan mountains. Despite its impressive height, it's still only about a medium-sized volcano for Mars, which is home much more impressively-sized volcanoes. For example, the planet's largest volcano Olympus Mons measures in at roughly 13.2 miles high (21.3 kilometers). Tharsis Tholus, a volcano on the surface of Mars, as seen by ESA's Mars Express orbiter. (Image credit: ESA/DLR/FU Berlin) Why is it incredible? While Tharsis Tholus might not be the tallest volcano on Mars, it is incredibly steep. It is steeper than Mauna Kea in Hawaii on Earth. To fully showcase the volcano's structure and topography in 3D, researchers actually exaggerated the vertical scale in this image, ESA reported . In addition to being steep and fairly tall, the volcano also has an interesting history. You can see that it is speckled with what look like small holes which are actually craters created by impacts from objects like asteroids. The volcano's current, unique shape is a combined effort by these impacts, environmental factors causing erosion and warping and ancient lava flows that left behind built-up material. The observations by Mars Express also reveals cracks and other imperfections in the volcano. All of these details might seem like superficial bits of detail, however every small crater, every lumpy cliffside and every worn down surface hides information about the planet's past. By studying features like volcanoes on Mars, researchers can piece together what the planet may have looked like in its ancient past. How active was this volcano? How did it interact with the landscape around it? Observations like this can hold the answers.

After a tortuous fortnight of negotiations, COP31 ended in disarray late on 22 November after countries including the UK and the EU refused to agree to a political accord that failed to mention fossil fuels. Read more Can everyone live a ‘good life’ without destroying the planet? The Antalya pact would have seen countries officially recognise that the world is on course to exceed 1.5°C degrees of warming and promise to limit the scale of the overshoot as far as possible. It also would have committed nations to increasing the share of electricity in total final energy consumption to 35 per cent globally by 2035, a key target for climate campaigners who see electrification as the route away from fossil-fuel dependency. Advertisement But the draft agreement proved unacceptable to many countries, including the UK, the EU and some small island nations, after all mentions of fossil fuels were omitted at the behest of fossil fuel-dependent nations such as Saudi Arabia and Russia. Failing to mention fossil fuels explicitly in the text would have marked a backwards step for the climate process, the EU argued. At COP28 in Dubai three years ago, nations agreed to “transition away from fossil fuels” , but since then, attempts to strengthen the language or clarify how this transition will take place have been blocked by petrostates. Alden Meyer at the climate think tank E3G says the talks were subjected to a “brutish” strategy from fossil fuel-exporting states to “systematically block” any reference to the COP28 deal. “They clearly have buyer’s remorse about that agreement. They never were happy about it.” Free newsletter Sign up to The Earth Edition Sign up to newsletter The EU also took issue with a paragraph inserted at the behest of Saudi Arabia – which leads the 22-member Arab group of countries – calling for the rapid growth of carbon capture and storage technologies to the gigatonne scale by 2035. Carbon capture and storage technologies are expensive and unproven at scale, and many sceptics are concerned that focusing on them will justify the continued use of fossil fuels and distract from the deep emissions cuts necessary for controlling climate change. science.description:
Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

On July 12, 1988, Phobos 2 — one of the Soviet Union's final major planetary exploration probes — was launched from Baikonur Cosmodrome aboard a Proton rocket. The spacecraft's mission included the study of Mars and the Martian moon Phobos, with a planned close approach and deployment of landing probes, and over the next several months, the spacecraft successfully captured more than three dozen images of Phobos during its time in service. However, early in the following year, the spacecraft's mission abruptly ended after the Phobos 2 ground team mysteriously lost contact with the spacecraft. Adding to the mystery were objects in some of the final photographs dispatched by the doomed spacecraft, which seemed to show an elongated shadow beneath the probe — a strange twist in one of the Soviet Union's final space missions, and one that soon gave rise to conspiracy theories about what the fate of Phobos 2 might have been. So what caused the odd-looking appearance of the shadow in the final images captured by Phobos 2, and what was the real reason behind the spacecraft's sudden failure? Last of the Soviet space explorers Originally, the Soviet Union had planned for Phobos 2 to reach the Red Planet by late January 1989, after which the spacecraft would begin collecting data about the Martian environment leading up to its initial contact with Mars' largest moon in early June. A model of one of the Phobos spacecraft on display in the Memorial Museum of Cosmonautics in Moscow, Russia. (Image credit: Музей Космонавтики from Россия, CC0, via Wikimedia Commons) To say that a lot hinged on the success of the mission would be an understatement, given the unfortunate fate of the probe's predecessor, Phobos 1, which went offline on Sept. 2, 1988, after a faulty command sequence was initiated while the spacecraft was on its way to Mars. The stakes were almost immediately raised as Phobos 2 arrived in orbit around Mars on Jan. 30, 1989 , when one of the probe's three onboard flight system processors was found to have gone offline, with another already experiencing technical issues. Over the course of the next several weeks, Phobos 2 was able to overcome some of these setbacks and successfully began sending useful scientific data about the Martian environment back to Earth. By March, all the probe's science instruments appeared to be functioning normally, and despite the earlier loss of one of its processors, the remaining two had continued to facilitate control of the spacecraft by its Soviet ground control team. science.title: Astronomers just discovered a rare triple star system 28 light-years away, and they have ‘no clean explanation for how it got here’
science.description: A triple system containing a dim red dwarf star and not one but two white dwarfs has been fortuitously discovered just 28 light-years away from our solar system. "We were actually looking for planets ," Étienne Artigau of the Trottier Institute for Research on Exoplanets at the Université de Montréal, who led the discovery, said in a statement . "Instead, we found something much more surprising." So surprising that there are no similar systems within at least 100 light-years . Furthermore, the configuration of the system seems impossible. "This system should not exist," added Montreal's Patrick Dufour. "We have no clean explanation for how it got here." This triple system has been called Welopō'ai, which is a portmanteau of two Hawaiian words that means a 'path of family traits', and to understand the mystery behind it requires astronomers to figure out the history of the three objects. A white dwarf is what remains when a star of similar mass to our sun reaches the end of its life. As it begins to run low on hydrogen for nuclear fusion reactions in its core, the star's energy generation begins to falter and its interior starts to contract under gravity . This has the effect of raising the temperature throughout the star, causing an outer shell of hydrogen to ignite its own fusion reactions. The star promptly bloats to become a red giant tens or even hundreds of millions of kilometers across. Soon enough the star ceases fusion reactions completely. The star's outer layers are shed and they expand out into space, while its core contracts to become an inert white dwarf with a diameter similar to Earth but with a mass generally between half and two-thirds of a solar mass . Therefore, the Welopō'ai system was once a triple system with two sun-like stars plus the red dwarf. Now the two sun-like stars have undergone this stage of star death while their companion red dwarf continues to linger, since its low mass bequeaths it a longer life because it does not use up its core hydrogen as quickly. One of the white dwarfs orbits the red dwarf at a distance of 129.3 astronomical units (19.3 billion kilometers or 12 billion miles) and takes about 1,000 years to complete one orbit. This white dwarf and the red dwarf were previously known, and Artigau's team had been using the SPectropolarimètre InfraROUge (SPIRou) instrument on the Canada–France–Hawaii Telescope atop Mauna Kea to search for planets orbiting the red dwarf when they noticed something highly unusual. By measuring the time it took for the light to return, they demonstrated a new, more precise method for tracking satellites. Since then, satellite laser ranging (SLR) has grown more precise and more widely used. The technique now underpins many aspects of Earth observation, such as validating satellite orbits and mapping subtle changes to Earth’s surface. Pioneered at the Goddard Optical Research Facility—now the Goddard Geophysical and Astronomical Observatory —laser ranging is performed at more than 40 stations worldwide.
